questions.text: Imagine a login form that directly builds a SQL query by joining strings. An attacker submits `' OR 1=1; --`. What is the attacker trying to do?

answers.text: Make the database return all rows or bypass authentication

questions.text: Which single change makes user input treated as data, not code?
True or False: Validating that a value is numeric is always enough to prevent SQL Injection.

answers.text: False — validation helps but is not a full defense

questions.text: Your Turn: Name one extra server-side control (not input validation) you should use to limit damage from SQL injection.

Level 2: Why do parameterized queries stop SQL injection?

answers.text: Because data is sent separately from the SQL command so it can't change SQL syntax
